findings.heading: **base** R
findings.proposition: The English marks '**base** R' as a level-2 section heading (## **base** R {}); the Turkish line carries the same text but no ## marker, so the section heading does not exist on the Turkish side.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader gets no section break: the base R part of the chapter renders as a stray bold line inside the 'Verileri ice aktar' (Import data) section, is absent from the table of contents and from section numbering, and its six sub-sections (T testleri, Shapiro-Wilk, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis, Ki-kare) appear to hang under Import data instead of under base R.

findings.heading: T-tests (base R)
findings.proposition: The English gives the three literal string values accepted by t.test's alternative argument as "two.sided", "less" and "greater"; the Turkish translates these literal R values into Turkish words ("iki tarafli", "daha az", "daha buyuk").
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader who follows the text and writes t.test(age_years ~ gender, data = linelist, alternative = "iki tarafli") gets an error, because t.test only matches the English strings. These are argument values passed to R, not labels, so they cannot be translated.

findings.heading: Wilcoxon rank sum test (base R)
findings.proposition: The Wilcoxon rank sum test is used to help determine whether two numeric samples come from the same distribution.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish sentence states only when the test is used (non-normal populations, unequal variance) and never states what it tests. A reader learns the precondition but not the hypothesis, so cannot say what the p-value beside the wilcox.test() chunk refers to.

findings.heading: `gtsummary` package
findings.proposition: A statistical test of comparison is performed with tbl_summary by ADDING the add_p function to the table.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish sentence is broken across three lines and loses the verb 'adding': it reads roughly 'to a table, the add_p function and which test will be used is specified'. The reader is not told that add_p must be appended to the tbl_summary pipeline, and must reverse-engineer that from the code chunks below.

findings.heading: Summary statistics (rstatix)
findings.proposition: The last of the default summary statistics returned by get_summary_stats() is a confidence interval OF THE MEAN.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish list ends with an unqualified 'guven araligi' (confidence interval). The output columns beside it are ci for the mean, so a reader may read the interval as applying to the median or to the whole distribution.

findings.heading: Correlations
findings.proposition: corrr can compute correlations by three named methods: Pearson, Kendall tau, or Spearman rho.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish breaks the list mid-way with a full stop, so it asserts that corrr computes correlations 'using Pearson Kendall' and strands 'tau veya Spearman rho,' as a fragment attached to the next sentence. A reader cannot tell that Kendall tau and Spearman rho are two separate selectable alternatives to the default Pearson used in the chunk below.
